source.title: WebOverlay: High-Throughput Vision-Only Distillation for Extreme Aspect-Ratio Web Overlay Detection
source.authors: Jian-Nan Huang; Jerry Ding; Liu Yu; Zhen-Ting Li

page_placements.theme: Student-over-supervisor gains from input asymmetry (privileged or degraded views), and bias from supervisor-assisted reference labels

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests teacher-label fine-tuning in vision-only web overlay detection, a modality and task outside the original language-focused settings.
record.gate_note: The study fine-tunes SigLIP on Gemini 2.5 Flash verdicts and reports student-versus-teacher outcomes. It does not calculate PGR or train a strong-model true-label ceiling. Other model baselines and most tiling/aggregation ablations are not rows unless they directly compare the weak-label student with its supervisor or test a training change.
record.test_reason: This is ordinary strong-to-compact distillation, not weak-to-strong. The supervisor (Gemini 2.5 Flash) is the more capable model, and the student (SigLIP-So400m with an MLP head) is a cheap compressed model. The paper frames the teacher as accurate and the student as cheaper, so no version's system (a strong student on a weaker supervisor's labels) is present. Where the student beats the teacher (blind long pages), the paper attributes this to an input-resolution asymmetry: the teacher sees a downscaled whole page, the student sees width-aligned crops. Scoring the teacher on the same three crops raises its ρ≥8 recall from 59.1% to 95.5%, with 100% recall and 84.8% F1 on blind Test-Hard. That is comparable to the student's 92.9%. The student's advantage is therefore confounded by input and does not show generalization beyond a weaker supervisor. Weak-to-strong appears only in related work, as an analogy ('Students can outperform their teachers').
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with additions. The authors conclude that the three-crop vision-only student nearly matches its MLLM teacher on standard pages. They find it surpasses the teacher on long pages under blind evaluation, which they attribute to the higher effective resolution of width-aligned tiling. They also conclude that teacher-prefilled annotation anchors labels toward the teacher, and that the student is about 83% cheaper to serve. They do not frame this as weak-to-strong generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a pretrained vision encoder fully fine-tuned on a weaker MLLM's binary verdicts, matching the weak-label-to-pretrained-strong-student setup at a high level. It is a vision task, uses a custom mixed hard-label/teacher-score loss, trains on whole-page images, and applies three-tile inference; it does not use the original PGR measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance depends on page aspect ratio and evaluation-label protocol: teacher-assisted labels favor the teacher, while blind hard-page evaluations favor the student. Full versus top-four-layer fine-tuning changes F1.

fits_no_version.finding: A compact SigLIP student distilled from Gemini 2.5 Flash verdicts matches the teacher on standard pages. On blind long pages it exceeds the teacher (86.5 vs 30.8 F1, p<0.001; 92.9 vs 63.6 on the paired subset), because at inference it sees higher-resolution crops than the teacher. When the teacher gets the same crops, its long-page recall recovers (59.1%→95.5%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilled students can exceed a stronger teacher on inputs where the teacher's view is degraded at inference: input-asymmetry gains, not weak-to-strong generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-filling annotators with teacher verdicts inflated teacher agreement on long pages (κ 0.59→0.88). It also reversed the student–teacher ordering seen under blind labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher-assisted reference labels bias student-versus-supervisor comparisons toward the supervisor.

record.problems: PGR and a strong model trained on true labels are not reported. The main in-set evaluation uses teacher-assisted labels; the paper documents anchoring bias and provides blind evaluations, but the independent hard slice has only 19 positive overlays. The fine-tuning-depth ablation has one training run per setting.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded non-distillation baselines and most inference-only tiling/aggregation ablations because they do not directly compare the weak-label student with its supervisor or test a training change. Also excluded the teacher scored on crops, since it changes the supervisor's input rather than measuring the weak-label student's result.

untested.parts: Not tested: no weaker supervisor, no PGR, no strong-student true-label ceiling.
Not tested: no confidence loss, supervisor ensembling, or PGR comparison against naive fine-tuning.
Not tested: there is no weak supervisor, so supervisor-exploitation and correlated-error tests do not apply.
Not tested: a vision task, but the supervisor is stronger than the student.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests classification is rejected: the teacher is the stronger model, and the student's wins are confounded by different inference inputs. The teacher-on-crops control (§4.3) is declared in rows_left_out, but it is the key result showing input, not student capability, drives the gap. A researcher should see it alongside r7–r8. Training labels come from the teacher on whole-page views, so the student does generalize beyond some teacher label errors on long pages. However, with a stronger teacher and changed test-time input, this cannot be read as V1 evidence.

versions.untested_parts: PGR itself and the strong model's true-label ceiling are not reported; much of the evidence is F1 or recall versus the teacher.
Tests full 27-layer versus top-four-layer fine-tuning, but not auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or the named loss variants; PGR is not reported.
Does not compare supervisor/student sizes, NLP/chess/reward-modelling tasks, or representation-based predictors of PGR.
Tests performance across aspect-ratio slices and an independent blind benchmark; does not test exploiting what the supervisor cannot check, correlated student/supervisor errors, or PGR under shift.
No theoretical conditions or guarantee are tested.
Tests one vision-only task and model setup; no other non-language modalities are tested.

relation.reason: §2.3 discusses weak-to-strong generalization and explicitly distinguishes its more capable pretrained student from this study's reversed input asymmetry.

tranche.reason: The study distills a commercial MLLM into a compact vision student; it does not establish a more capable pretrained student learning from a weaker supervisor. Its teacher-on-crops control attributes long-page gains to input resolution.

source_check.notes: Matching on standard pages refers to blind Val-Common; teacher-assisted Test-Common instead favors the teacher significantly. Tiling is applied only at inference; the teacher-on-crops control supports the resolution explanation.
